segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now he was praying in a certain place, and when he finished, one of his disciples said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “When you pray, say: ‘Father, may your name be held holy. May your kingdom come.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Give us each day our daily bread.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And forgive us our sins, for we ourselves forgive everyone who is indebted to us. And do not bring us into testing.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Which of you will have a friend and go to him at midnight and say to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: because a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him’;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and he will answer from inside, ‘Do not bother me. The door is already shut, and my children are with me in bed. I cannot get up and give you anything’?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I tell you, even if he will not get up and give him anything because he is his friend, yet because of his shamelessness he will rise and give him as much as he needs.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And I tell you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Which father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will hand him a snake instead of a fish?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Or if he asks for an egg, will hand him a scorpion?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you then, evil as you are, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was casting out a demon that was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke, and the crowds were amazed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But some of them said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He casts out the demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Others, to test him, were seeking from him a sign from heaven.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls upon house.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if Satan too is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out the demons by Beelzebul.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But if I cast out the demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But if it is by the finger of God that I cast out the demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own palace, his possessions are safe.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But when someone stronger than he attacks and overcomes him, he takes away the armor on which he relied and divides up his spoils.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When the unclean spirit goes out of a person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and finding none it says, ‘I will return to my house that I came out of.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And when it comes, it finds the house swept and put in order.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then it goes and brings along seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and settle there; and the last state of that person becomes worse than the first.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Blessed is the womb that carried you, and the breasts that nursed you!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and keep it!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As the crowds were growing, he began to say,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This generation is an evil generation. It seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so also the Son of Man will be to this generation.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The queen of the South will be raised at the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and look, something greater than Solomon is here.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because they turned back at the proclamation of Jonah, and look, something greater than Jonah is here.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on the lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The lamp of the body is your eye. When your eye is generous, your whole body also is full of light; but when it is stingy, your body also is dark.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: See to it, then, that the light in you is not darkness.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If then your whole body is full of light, with no part of it dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp illuminates you with its brightness.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he had spoken, a Pharisee asked him to have a meal at his house; so he went in and reclined at table.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Pharisee was amazed when he saw that he did not first wash before the meal.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the Lord said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Fools! Did not the one who made the outside make the inside also?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But give what is inside as alms, and look, everything is clean for you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every garden herb, and pass over justice and the love of God. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the front seat in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Woe to you! For you are like unmarked tombs, and the people who walk over them do not know it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of the experts in the law answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, in saying these things you insult us too.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Woe to you experts in the law as well! For you load people with burdens hard to carry, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and it was your ancestors who killed them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So you are witnesses, and you approve of the deeds of your ancestors, because they killed them and you build.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For this reason also the Wisdom of God said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute,’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: so that this generation may be held accountable for the blood of all the prophets shed since the foundation of the world,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, this generation will be held accountable for it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Woe to you experts in the law! For you have taken away the key of knowledge. You did not go in yourselves, and you hindered those who were going in.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he went out from there, the scribes and the Pharisees began to oppose him fiercely and to interrogate him about many things,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: lying in wait for him, to catch him in something out of his own mouth.

notes.traditional: Our Father who art in heaven
notes.note: Luke's form of the prayer is shorter than Matthew's. Many later manuscripts expand it toward the Matthean wording ('Our Father in the heavens', 'your will be done', 'rescue us from the evil one'), but the earliest witnesses lack these lines, and the short form is translated here.

notes.phrase: may your name be held holy
notes.note: 'Hallowed' is the traditional word and means exactly this, but it is no longer in ordinary use. The verb asks that God's name be treated as holy; the passive probably implies that God himself is asked to bring this about.

The Greek word is almost unknown outside the Lord's Prayer, and its meaning is genuinely uncertain. The main proposals are 'for the coming day', 'necessary for existence' and 'for today'. The traditional 'daily' is kept because no alternative is secure.

The Greek word covers both a trial that tests faithfulness and an enticement to sin; in the Septuagint and in this period the first sense is the more usual. Most translations keep 'temptation', and some give 'time of trial'. The same word family appears in verse 16, where people 'test' Jesus.

In Greek usage of the period the word means lack of shame, impudence; evidence that it meant 'persistence' is weak, though many translations render it so in light of the parable's use. It is usually taken as the nerve of the man who knocks at midnight. Some scholars refer it instead to the man in bed, who acts to avoid being shamed for refusing a neighbour.

The phrase echoes Exodus 8:19, where Pharaoh's magicians, unable to match a plague, admit, 'This is the finger of God.' It means God's own direct power at work. The parallel in Matthew 12:28 has 'the Spirit of God'.

The Greek particle can correct ('No, rather'), or affirm and go further ('Yes, but even more'). The rendering leaves this open as far as English allows. Most interpreters think Jesus does not deny the woman's words but redirects them to what matters more.

'Repent' in modern English centres on feeling sorry. The Greek word here carries the prophets' call to return to God, a change of direction in mind and conduct, which is what the people of Nineveh did in the book of Jonah. Most translations keep 'repent' as an established term understood to include a change of life.

The word literally means 'single' or 'sound', and most translations render it 'healthy', keeping the physical picture of the eye. In Jewish idiom a 'good eye' is generosity and an 'evil eye' is grudging stinginess; 'stingy' here renders the ordinary Greek word for 'evil'. This translation follows the idiom, at the cost of the physical image, and the mainstream rendering remains defensible, particularly in Luke, where the surrounding context is about light rather than money.

The verb is the one usually rendered 'baptize'. Here it refers to a ritual washing before eating, a matter of purity rather than hygiene, which Pharisaic tradition required though the Law of Moses did not command it of ordinary people at ordinary meals.

notes.phrase: give what is inside as alms
notes.note: The Greek is compressed. It is taken here to mean giving away the contents of the cup and dish to the poor. Others understand 'as for what is inside, give alms', or 'give alms from within', that is, from the heart. 'Alms' are charitable gifts to those in need.

Under the Law, contact with a grave made a person ritually unclean for seven days (Numbers 19:16), so graves were marked to warn passers-by. Anyone walking over an unmarked one became unclean without knowing it. The charge is that the Pharisees, who were devoted to purity, were themselves a hidden source of defilement.

'Lawyer' now suggests an attorney who represents clients in court. These were specialists in interpreting the Law of Moses and its application to daily life. Several modern translations already use 'experts in the law'.

No known passage of Scripture contains these words. The phrase may personify God's wisdom as a speaker, as Proverbs does, or it may refer to a writing now lost, or to God's wise decree; in Matthew 23:34 the saying is given in Jesus' own voice. Where the quotation ends is also uncertain; it is closed here at the end of verse 49.

notes.phrase: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah
notes.note: Abel is the first person murdered in Genesis. Zechariah is usually identified with the priest stoned in the temple court in 2 Chronicles 24:20–22; in the arrangement of the Hebrew Scriptures that places Chronicles last, the pair spans the first and last murders in Scripture. 'The sanctuary' renders the Greek 'the house', meaning the temple building.

candidates.reason: It recurs across the Gospels and letters, and the choice between 'temptation', 'testing' and 'trial' changes how the Lord's Prayer and many other passages read.
It is frequent in the Gospels and Revelation; 'woe' is archaic, the alternatives ('how terrible for', 'alas for') differ in tone, and the choice should be uniform.
'Lawyer' misleads modern readers, and the rendering needs to be coordinated with γραμματεύς so the two groups stay distinct.
It is very frequent in the Gospels and Acts; translations vary between 'scribe', 'teacher of the law' and 'legal scholar', and 'scribe' may suggest a mere copyist.
It recurs in Matthew, Luke and Acts; 'alms' is fading from English, and the alternatives ('charity', 'gifts to the poor') should be chosen once.
